policy.reviewDueAt: Recheck volatile capabilities after this date before relying on them as current.

data.title: Turn current research into a decision memo
data.summary: Compare options with traceable claims, conflicting evidence and an explicit decision criterion.

facts.text: ChatGPT offers web search and deep research in Work; entry points and availability differ between web and desktop.

prerequisites: Access to ChatGPT Work with deep research; check account, client and workspace availability.
Name the question, audience, geography, date range and acceptable sources.
steps: Define the decision, cutoff date and criteria before collecting sources.
Use the web Deep research control or desktop Deep research plugin if available. Reuse authorized sources and record inaccessible ones.
Build a claim table with source URL, date, evidence and counter-evidence. Prefer original documents.
Compare options against the criteria; separate observations from your recommendation.
Open important citations and check that they support the claim. Deliver a memo with uncertainties.
data.output: a cited decision memo and claim/source table
validation: Preserve both dates and definitions; explain the unresolved conflict.
Remove or qualify the claim; do not substitute an unrelated citation.
limitations: Sintra-authored procedure based on provider documentation or demonstrations; no execution in the named app was performed.
Availability and results depend on your inputs, enabled tools and permissions; a suggested practice result is not a measured outcome.
data.prompt: Research [decision] for [audience, geography and cutoff date]. Reuse [existing source set]. First propose comparison criteria and research scope. Build a claim table with direct source URLs, publication dates, counter-evidence and confidence limits. Compare [options] and draft a concise recommendation, explaining what evidence would change it. Open important sources; mark inaccessible sources and unsupported claims. Do not contact anyone or make the decision for me.
tips: Ask what evidence would reverse the recommendation.
Specify a research cutoff so an old announcement is not treated as current availability.
